For a fixed Psi of dimension d, the fraction of dimension-g Weil polynomials divisible by Psi is about 2^{[(g-d)(g-d+1)-g(g+1)]/4} = 2^{-d(2g-d+1)/4}. That fraction SHRINKS as g grows, while the number of curves grows only as 2^{3g-3} (hyperelliptic: 2^{2g}). Expected hits are about 2^{3g - d(2g-d)/4}. This is maximised at g=d and is negative for every g in (d,2d] once d>12. At d=130 the best exponent is about -3835 at g=130 and about -11895 at g=260. Allowing a larger genus therefore makes the rarity worse, not better. The Prym map has image of dimension at most 3g'-3 in A_{g'-1}, and the curve family is still o(g^2) in dimension, so the same count applies (Torelli plus Prym codimension is quadratic in d).
